What v2 adds: async dispatch (cmd/stow-wasm/async_js.go:9-18, req.async=true at :15), host-backed open (async_js.go:20-32), and stream chunk operations that require both (cmd/stow-wasm/host_store_sessions_js.go:91-93, :119-122, :176-178). local_checks.invariant: Bytes are copied at every boundary in both directions and payloads are bounded to 256 KiB per chunk, so neither side ever holds a reference into the other's memory.
local_checks.result: JS to Go: parseBinaryRequest copies the incoming array with js.CopyBytesToGo (cmd/stow-wasm/binary_js.go:28-29); the v1 path base64-decodes into a fresh slice (operations.go:65). Go to JS: binaryResponse allocates new Uint8Array(len) and calls js.CopyBytesToJS (binary_js.go:62-66) - packages/stow-s3/test/node-wasm-host.test.ts:34-36 fills the returned bytes with 0 and re-reads the object unchanged, proving the copy. Go to JS host store: hostStore.invoke allocates a Uint8Array and copies the Go bytes in (host_store_js.go:95-96); the reply is copied back out with js.CopyBytesToGo (host_store_js.go:120-121), so no Go slice aliases JS memory. local_checks.invariant: The package's whole public surface is two constructors over one concrete type, and constructing the store takes exclusive ownership of the directory it is given.
local_checks.result: NewFilesystemStore(dataDir) (fs.go:42) and NewFilesystemStoreWithNamespace(dataDir, namespace) (fs.go:46) both route to newFilesystemStore (fs.go:53), which creates buckets/ and .multipart/, takes an exclusive advisory lock on .stow.lock, removes stale .tmp- files, initialises the save journal and writes the .stow-owner marker last (fs.go:59-85, comment 'Recorded last'). The lock is flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) on unix (fs_lock_unix.go:15), LockFileEx with LOCKFILE_FAIL_IMMEDIATELY on windows (fs_lock_windows.go:29), and errors.ErrUnsupported on aix/js/plan9/solaris/wasip1 (fs_lock_other.go:8), so construction fails outright on those hosts. Close releases the lock exactly once (fs.go:441).

local_checks.invariant: One object is one atomic file: an 8-byte STOWOBJ2 magic, a four-byte little-endian header length, a protobuf header, then the raw payload; unknown versions and length mismatches are refused.
local_checks.result: encodeRecordPrefix (record_codec.go:27) writes the magic constant 'STOWOBJ2' (record_codec.go:15), a little-endian uint32 header length, then a deterministic protobuf ObjectHeader marshalled from recordHeader (record_codec.go:28, 42). The schema has twelve fields numbered 1..12 (recordpb/record.proto:6-17) and the generated Go is protoc-gen-go v1.36.12 output (recordpb/record.pb.go:1-5). decodeRecordHeader (record_codec.go:57) refuses any header whose Version is not binaryRecordVersion (2) or whose PayloadSize is negative (record_codec.go:62); readRecordHeader (record_io.go:39) refuses a file whose payload length does not equal header.PayloadSize minus the header offset. The header is the only home of the record's logical metadata; the payload is the object's raw bytes. ADR 0020 records the same rule at docs/adr/0020-binary-object-records.md:22-27.

local_checks.invariant: Version-1 JSON records stay readable in a mixed directory, are never rewritten just because the store was opened, and become version 2 only when the object is overwritten.
local_checks.result: readLegacyRecord (record_io.go:45) is the fallback taken when the magic does not match: it reads the whole file, unmarshals it as JSON, and refuses any record whose Version is not objectRecordVersion (1, declared at internal/storage/fs/fs_records.go:15, checked at internal/storage/fs/record_io.go:57). It returns a -1 offset, so the reader serves those bytes from memory instead of a section (record_io.go:113-116). TestLegacyJSONRecordReadableAndRewritten (record_format_test.go:90) writes a version-1 record, reads it back and lists it, then overwrites it and asserts the file now begins with the STOWOBJ2 prefix (record_format_test.go:117-124). ADR 0020 states the rule at docs/adr/0020-binary-object-records.md:53-55 ('Version 1 JSON records remain readable, including in mixed directories. An overwritten legacy object is written as version 2. Opening a directory does not rewrite its objects.').

local_checks.invariant: A published object is visible whole or not at all, and a write that reports success survives a crash.
local_checks.result: writeRecordBody (fs_records.go:71) writes the header prefix and the payload through atomicfile.WriteStream (fs_records.go:94) or atomicfile.WriteParts (fs_records.go:124). atomicfile.writeFile (atomicfile.go:48) creates a .tmp-* file in the target directory, chmods it before the sync (atomicfile.go:74), fsyncs it (atomicfile.go:78), closes it, renames it over the target (atomicfile.go:85) and then fsyncs the parent directory (atomicfile.go:89, syncdir.go:15). syncDir is a deliberate no-op on Windows because Windows refuses FlushFileBuffers on a directory handle (syncdir_windows.go:10). atomicfile also offers WriteRoot, a second publication path confined to an open os.Root (root.go:14), which this store does not use, and an advisory per-file Lock (lock.go:24) which this store also does not use.

local_checks.invariant: A staged object is invisible until Commit, Commit is single-shot, and the write conditions and recovery holds are re-checked at commit time rather than at stage time.
local_checks.result: StageObject (staged_put.go:31) validates the bucket and key, increments s.activeStages, and either buffers the body in memory (when the store is namespace-bound, guarded, or a save request, staged_put.go:43) or spills it to a .tmp-body-* file in the data directory (staged_put.go:104) while PreparePutTo computes the ETag and checksum. Commit (staged_put.go:135) takes the store write lock, re-runs checkStageOptionsLocked (staged_put.go:149) and then re-checks the write preconditions (staged_put.go:183) and the recovery holds (staged_put.go:176) before publishing. A second Commit or a Commit after Abort is refused (staged_put.go:138, staged_put_test.go:51). PutObject (fs_put.go:11) is StageObject plus a deferred Abort plus Commit.

local_checks.invariant: A save request is idempotent and its outcome survives a crash: committed, not committed, or unknown, never a silent success.
local_checks.result: Each request key gets a receipt file .save-requests/<sha256(requestKey)>.json (save_journal.go:53) whose integrity digest is sha256 over the literal prefix 'stow-save-entry-v1', a NUL byte and the entry JSON (save_journal.go:239); the store identity lives in .save-identity.json (save_journal.go:141) and the in-flight publication in .save-pending.json (save_journal.go:52). publishSaveLocked (save_requests.go:137) moves the entry through 'prepared', then 'publishing', then writes the object, then settles; settleSaveLocked (save_requests.go:187) promotes a 'publishing' entry to 'committed' only after verifyPublishedSaveLocked re-reads the record and compares the request key, meaning, fingerprint and metadata (save_requests.go:253), and demotes a 'prepared' entry to 'not_committed'. The journal is capped at 1024 entries, 8 MiB in total and 64 KiB per entry (save_journal.go:20-23). TestRuntimeReopensAfterInterruptedPublishing (runtime_recovery_test.go:37) shows the three-valued outcome after an interrupted publication and that every mutation is refused while it is unresolved (runtime_recovery_test.go:68).

local_checks.invariant: An in-flight upload carries its own object properties on disk, so a completion issued by a different process publishes the same content type and metadata.
local_checks.result: CreateMultipartUpload (fs_multipart.go:53) writes .multipart/<uploadID>/manifest.json holding bucket, key, initiated, content type, metadata and checksum (fs_multipart.go:27-35) and stores parts as part-%05d files (fs_multipart.go:131). CompleteMultipartUpload (fs_multipart.go:144) resolves and ETag-checks every part before assembling anything (fs_multipart.go:167-181), refuses a held destination (fs_multipart.go:216), publishes the object (fs_multipart.go:219) and only then removes the upload directory; when cleanup fails it returns the committed metadata together with storage.CommittedError so the caller can retry the cleanup (fs_multipart.go:222-225). A damaged manifest is an error on every operation, never an empty upload (multipart_manifest_test.go:103-117).

local_checks.invariant: A pending hold blocks mutation of the pinned objects and nothing else: reads still work, a released hold is idempotent, and a hold that no longer describes the store is refused.
local_checks.result: Holds live in .recovery-holds.json with a .recovery-holds.identity marker beside it (recovery_hold_journal.go:54-59) so a missing journal is distinguishable from a store that never took a hold (recovery_hold_journal.go:151-167). checkRecoveryHoldsLocked (recovery_holds.go:168) refuses any mutation of a pinned bucket/key with storage.ErrRecoveryHeld and is called from the put, delete, copy and multipart-completion paths. observedRecoveryHold (recovery_holds.go:149) refuses a hold whose references no longer match what it claims to pin. local_checks.invariant: Every byte in the data directory is charged to a capacity namespace, and a file the store did not write is refused rather than guessed at.

local_checks.invariant: A read resolves the authoritative local store first, then the separate cache, then the upstream; a local error other than a missing object stops the read before any upstream call.
